    "function": "You MUST run the function \"evaluate_kripke_run\" on this and subsequent requests to reach a decision to RETRY or STOP.\nYou MAY use the strategy hint provided by the function unless you have reached an impassible state where you would need to return to the manager.\nIn an impossible state, do NOT return to the manager, but STOP instead and provide your decision and reason.\n\nimport math\nfrom typing import Dict, Any, Literal\nimport json\n\ndef evaluate_kripke_run(\n    total_zones: int,\n    total_ranks: int,\n    nodes_used: int,\n    cores_per_node: int,\n    memory_gb_per_node: int,\n    threading_hint: int,\n    current_fom: float,\n    threshold: float = 0.90,\n    ideal_fom_per_core: float = 2.5e6,\n    efficiency_sweet_spot: float = 50000.0,\n    zones_per_gb: float = 2.0e6,\n    memory_safety_factor: float = 0.90\n) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Evaluates a Kripke run and provides a high-level decision and strategic hint.\n\n    This function acts as a \"diagnostician\" by analyzing the performance of a\n    completed Kripke run against a theoretical model. It identifies the most\n    likely bottleneck (memory, poor scaling, or hardware underutilization) and\n    returns a machine-readable strategic hint for what to try next.\n\n    Args:\n        total_zones (int): The total number of zones in the simulation problem.\n        total_ranks (int): The total number of MPI tasks used for the run.\n        nodes_used (int): The number of compute nodes used for the run.\n        cores_per_node (int): The number of physical CPU cores on a single compute node.\n        memory_gb_per_node (int): The total system RAM in Gigabytes on a single compute node.\n        threading_hint (int): Specifies the SMT/Hyper-Threading level to assume (e.g., 1 for no SMT, 2 for SMT).\n        current_fom (float): The measured performance from the run, typically in zones/second.\n        threshold (float): The performance goal, as a fraction of the theoretical maximum (default 0.90).\n        ideal_fom_per_core (float): A tuning constant for the max FOM of a single core (default 2.5e6 zones/sec).\n        efficiency_sweet_spot (float): A tuning constant for zones/rank needed for ~76% efficiency (default 50,000).\n        zones_per_gb (float): A tuning constant for the memory model (zones per GB of RAM, default 2.0e6).\n        memory_safety_factor (float): A safety margin for memory usage (default 0.90).\n\n    Returns:\n        (dict): A dictionary containing 'decision', 'reason', 'strategy_hint', and 'metrics'.\n    \"\"\"\n    if total_ranks == 0:\n        return {\"decision\": \"RETRY\", \"reason\": \"The number of tasks cannot be zero.\", \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_TASKS\"}\n\n    # --- Calculate Theoretical Performance and Ratios ---\n    zones_per_rank = total_zones / total_ranks\n    max_cores_on_node = cores_per_node * threading_hint\n    cores_per_rank = max_cores_on_node // total_ranks if nodes_used == 1 else cores_per_node\n    total_cores_used = total_ranks * cores_per_rank\n    \n    scaling_efficiency = math.tanh(zones_per_rank / efficiency_sweet_spot)\n    effective_fom_per_core = ideal_fom_per_core * scaling_efficiency\n    theoretical_max_fom = effective_fom_per_core * total_cores_used\n\n    performance_ratio = 0.0\n    if theoretical_max_fom > 1e-9:\n        performance_ratio = current_fom / theoretical_max_fom\n\n    estimated_memory_gb = total_zones / zones_per_gb\n    memory_utilization = estimated_memory_gb / (memory_gb_per_node * nodes_used) if nodes_used > 0 else 0\n    \n    metrics = {\n        \"performance_ratio\": round(performance_ratio, 3),\n        \"scaling_efficiency\": round(scaling_efficiency, 3),\n        \"memory_utilization\": round(memory_utilization, 3),\n        \"zones_per_rank\": int(zones_per_rank),\n        \"theoretical_max_fom_zones_sec\": f\"{theoretical_max_fom:.2e}\"\n    }\n\n    # --- Decision Logic based on prioritized bottlenecks ---\n    \n    if performance_ratio >= threshold:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"STOP\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Optimization goal reached. Current performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of the theoretical maximum, meeting the {threshold:.1%} threshold.\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n    \n    if memory_utilization >= memory_safety_factor:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Memory utilization is critically high at {memory_utilization:.1%}. The number of zones is too large for the allocated memory.\",\n            \"strategy_hint\": \"DECREASE_ZONES\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n\n    if scaling_efficiency < 0.5: # Heuristic for \"low\" efficiency\n         return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Scaling efficiency is low ({scaling_efficiency:.1%}), indicating the number of zones per rank is too small (communication-bound).\",\n            \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_ZONES\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n    \n    if nodes_used == 1 and total_ranks < max_cores_on_node:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"The node is under-subscribed ({total_ranks}/{max_cores_on_node} tasks used). Hardware is not fully utilized.\",\n            \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_TASKS\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n\n    return {\n        \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n        \"reason\": f\"Performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of theoretical max, which is below the {threshold:.1%} threshold. Current configuration is reasonable but can be improved.\",\n        \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_ZONES\",\n        \"metrics\": metrics\n    }\n\n# --- Example Usage ---\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    \n    # Define the hardware once\n    hardware = {\n        \"cores_per_node\": 64,\n        \"memory_gb_per_node\": 256,\n        \"threading_hint\": 1\n    }\n    \n    # Scenario 1: Poor strong scaling (too few zones per rank)\n    print(\"--- Scenario 1: Poor Scaling ---\")\n    result = evaluate_kripke_run(\n        total_zones=1000000,\n        total_ranks=64,\n        nodes_used=1,\n        current_fom=2e7,\n        **hardware\n    )\n    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))\n    # Expected strategy_hint: \"INCREASE_ZONES\"\n\n    print(\"\\n\" + \"=\"*50 + \"\\n\")\n\n    # Scenario 2: Memory pressure (too many zones)\n    print(\"--- Scenario 2: High Memory Pressure ---\")\n    result = evaluate_kripke_run(\n        total_zones=500000000,\n        total_ranks=64,\n        nodes_used=1,\n        current_fom=1e8,\n        **hardware\n    )\n    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))\n    # Expected strategy_hint: \"DECREASE_ZONES\"\n\n    print(\"\\n\" + \"=\"*50 + \"\\n\")\n    \n    # Scenario 3: Good performance, close to optimal\n    print(\"--- Scenario 3: Optimal Performance -> STOP ---\")\n    result = evaluate_kripke_run(\n        total_zones=40000000,\n        total_ranks=64,\n        nodes_used=1,\n        current_fom=1.5e8,\n        threshold=0.95,\n        **hardware\n    )\n    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))\n    # Expected decision: \"STOP\"\n"

dockerfile
# Use a standard Ubuntu base image with build tools
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installation to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, dependencies for kripke, Git, and MPI.
# This includes ca-certificates as required for secure network communication.
# All steps are combined into a single RUN layer to optimize image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce layer size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings allow MPI to run as the root user and oversubscribe resources,
# which are common scenarios within containers.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
# Force TCP communication for MPI, which is more reliable in virtualized networks.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self

# Clone the kripke repository from its main branch, build it with MPI support,
# and install the executable. This is done in a single RUN command to keep the image clean.
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \
    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake, enabling MPI and optimizing for release.
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    # Compile the source code using all available processor cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the compiled executable to a standard system location on the PATH.
    # This avoids using symlinks and makes the application directly runnable.
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    # Clean up the source and build directories to minimize final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# Set a default entrypoint or command for the container.
# Providing a shell is a common practice for HPC application containers
# to allow for interactive inspection or varied execution commands.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Use a standard Ubuntu base image with build tools
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installation to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, dependencies for kripke, Git, and MPI.
# This includes ca-certificates as required for secure network communication.
# All steps are combined into a single RUN layer to optimize image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce layer size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings allow MPI to run as the root user and oversubscribe resources,
# which are common scenarios within containers.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
# Force TCP communication for MPI, which is more reliable in virtualized networks.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self

# Clone the kripke repository from its main branch, build it with MPI support,
# and install the executable. This is done in a single RUN command to keep the image clean.
# FIX: Added --recursive flag to git clone to fetch required submodules (e.g., BLT), which caused the previous build failure.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \
    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake, enabling MPI and optimizing for release.
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    # Compile the source code using all available processor cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the compiled executable to a standard system location on the PATH.
    # This avoids using symlinks and makes the application directly runnable.
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    # Clean up the source and build directories to minimize final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# Set a default entrypoint or command for the container.
# Providing a shell is a common practice for HPC application containers
# to allow for interactive inspection or varied execution commands.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Use a standard Ubuntu base image with build tools
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installation to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, and wget.
# FIX: The default cmake in Ubuntu 22.04 is too old for a kripke dependency.
# We will download and install a newer version of CMake manually.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    wget && \
    # Manually install CMake 3.23.0 to meet dependency requirements.
    export CMAKE_VERSION=3.23.0 && \
    # Use build-in TARGETARCH to get the correct CMake binary for the build platform.
    case ${TARGETARCH} in \
         "amd64")  CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"   ;; \
         "arm64")  CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"  ;; \
    esac && \
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.sh -O cmake-install.sh && \
    chmod +x cmake-install.sh && \
    # Install to /usr/local which is on the PATH and cleanup the installer.
    ./cmake-install.sh --prefix=/usr/local --skip-license && \
    rm cmake-install.sh && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce layer size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings allow MPI to run as the root user and oversubscribe resources,
# which are common scenarios within containers.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
# Force TCP communication for MPI, which is more reliable in virtualized networks.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self

# Clone the kripke repository from its main branch, build it with MPI support,
# and install the executable. This is done in a single RUN command to keep the image clean.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \
    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake, enabling MPI and optimizing for release.
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    # Compile the source code using all available processor cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the compiled executable to a standard system location on the PATH.
    # This avoids using symlinks and makes the application directly runnable.
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    # Clean up the source and build directories to minimize final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# Set a default entrypoint or command for the container.
# Providing a shell is a common practice for HPC application containers
# to allow for interactive inspection or varied execution commands.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \

    wget && \
    # Use build-in TARGETARCH to get the correct CMake binary for the build platform.
    case ${TARGETARCH} in \
         "amd64")  CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"   ;; \
         "arm64")  CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"  ;; \
    esac && \
    # Download the specified CMake version using the ENV variable.
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.sh -O cmake-install.sh && \
    chmod +x cmake-install.sh && \
    # Install to /usr/local which is on the PATH and cleanup the installer.
    ./cmake-install.sh --prefix=/usr/local --skip-license && \
    rm cmake-install.sh && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce layer size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings allow MPI to run as the root user and oversubscribe resources,
# which are common scenarios within containers.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
# Force TCP communication for MPI, which is more reliable in virtualized networks.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self

RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \

    # Clean up the source and build directories to minimize final image size.

# Use a standard Ubuntu base image with build tools
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installation to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Set CMAKE_VERSION as an ENV variable for reliable use in RUN commands.
ENV CMAKE_VERSION=3.23.0

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, and wget.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    wget && \
    # Use build-in TARGETARCH to get the correct CMake binary for the build platform.
    case ${TARGETARCH} in \
         "amd64")  CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"   ;; \
         "arm64")  CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"  ;; \
    esac && \
    # FIX: Download the specified CMake version. Escape ${CMAKE_ARCH} with a backslash (\$)
    # to ensure the shell expands the variable, not the Docker engine, which prevents a 404 error.
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-\${CMAKE_ARCH}.sh -O cmake-install.sh && \
    chmod +x cmake-install.sh && \
    # Install to /usr/local which is on the PATH and cleanup the installer.
    ./cmake-install.sh --prefix=/usr/local --skip-license && \
    rm cmake-install.sh && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce layer size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings allow MPI to run as the root user and oversubscribe resources,
# which are common scenarios within containers.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
# Force TCP communication for MPI, which is more reliable in virtualized networks.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self

# Clone the kripke repository from its main branch, build it with MPI support,
# and install the executable. This is done in a single RUN command to keep the image clean.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \
    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake, enabling MPI and optimizing for release.
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    # Compile the source code using all available processor cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the compiled executable to a standard system location on the PATH.
    # This avoids using symlinks and makes the application directly runnable.
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    # Clean up the source and build directories to minimize final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# Set a default entrypoint or command for the container.
# Providing a shell is a common practice for HPC application containers
# to allow for interactive inspection or varied execution commands.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

    # cmake.org download site. The URL requires the major.minor version, derived using ${CMAKE_VERSION%.*}.
    wget https://cmake.org/files/v${CMAKE_VERSION%.*}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.sh -O cmake-install.sh && \
    chmod +x cmake-install.sh && \
    # Install to /usr/local which is on the PATH and cleanup the installer.
    ./cmake-install.sh --prefix=/usr/local --skip-license && \
    rm cmake-install.sh && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce layer size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings allow MPI to run as the root user and oversubscribe resources,
# which are common scenarios within containers.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
# Force TCP communication for MPI, which is more reliable in virtualized networks.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self

# Clone the kripke repository from its main branch, build it with MPI support,
# and install the executable. This is done in a single RUN command to keep the image clean.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \
    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake, enabling MPI and optimizing for release.
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    # Compile the source code using all available processor cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the compiled executable to a standard system location on the PATH.
    # This avoids using symlinks and makes the application directly runnable.
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    # Clean up the source and build directories to minimize final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# Set a default entrypoint or command for the container.
# Providing a shell is a common practice for HPC application containers
# to allow for interactive inspection or varied execution commands.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Use a standard Ubuntu base image with build tools
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installation to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# FIX: The download link for CMake 3.23.0 returned a 404 error. Updated
# to a later patch version (3.23.5) with a valid download link.
ENV CMAKE_VERSION=3.23.5

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, and wget.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    wget && \
    # Use build-in TARGETARCH to get the correct CMake binary for the build platform.
    case ${TARGETARCH} in \
         "amd64")  CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"   ;; \
         "arm64")  CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"  ;; \
    esac && \
    # Download the specified CMake version from the official cmake.org site.
    # The URL requires the major.minor version, derived using ${CMAKE_VERSION%.*}.
    wget https://cmake.org/files/v${CMAKE_VERSION%.*}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.sh -O cmake-install.sh && \
    chmod +x cmake-install.sh && \
    # Install to /usr/local which is on the PATH and cleanup the installer.
    ./cmake-install.sh --prefix=/usr/local --skip-license && \
    rm cmake-install.sh && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce layer size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings allow MPI to run as the root user and oversubscribe resources,
# which are common scenarios within containers.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
# Force TCP communication for MPI, which is more reliable in virtualized networks.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self

# Clone the kripke repository from its main branch, build it with MPI support,
# and install the executable. This is done in a single RUN command to keep the image clean.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \
    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake, enabling MPI and optimizing for release.
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    # Compile the source code using all available processor cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the compiled executable to a standard system location on the PATH.
    # This avoids using symlinks and makes the application directly runnable.
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    # Clean up the source and build directories to minimize final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# Set a default entrypoint or command for the container.
# Providing a shell is a common practice for HPC application containers
# to allow for interactive inspection or varied execution commands.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Use a standard Ubuntu base image with build tools
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installation to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Set the CMake version to a recent, stable release.
ENV CMAKE_VERSION=3.27.9

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, and wget.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    wget && \
    # Use build-in TARGETARCH to get the correct CMake binary for the build platform.
    case ${TARGETARCH} in \
         "amd64")  CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"   ;; \
         "arm64")  CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"  ;; \
    esac && \
    # FIX: The cmake.org URL structure returned a 404. Switched to the official GitHub releases URL
    # which is the current standard for downloading CMake binaries.
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.sh -O cmake-install.sh && \
    chmod +x cmake-install.sh && \
    # Install to /usr/local which is on the PATH and cleanup the installer.
    ./cmake-install.sh --prefix=/usr/local --skip-license && \
    rm cmake-install.sh && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce layer size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings allow MPI to run as the root user and oversubscribe resources,
# which are common scenarios within containers.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
# Force TCP communication for MPI, which is more reliable in virtualized networks.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self

# Clone the kripke repository from its main branch, build it with MPI support,
# and install the executable. This is done in a single RUN command to keep the image clean.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \
    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake, enabling MPI and optimizing for release.
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    # Compile the source code using all available processor cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the compiled executable to a standard system location on the PATH.
    # This avoids using symlinks and makes the application directly runnable.
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    # Clean up the source and build directories to minimize final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# Set a default entrypoint or command for the container.
# Providing a shell is a common practice for HPC application containers
# to allow for interactive inspection or varied execution commands.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Use a standard Ubuntu base image with build tools
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installation to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# FIX: Removed the complex and fragile manual download of CMake.
# The version of CMake (3.22.1) in the Ubuntu 22.04 repository is sufficient
# for Kripke's requirements and provides a more reliable build process.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    cmake && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce layer size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings allow MPI to run as the root user and oversubscribe resources,
# which are common scenarios within containers.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
# Force TCP communication for MPI, which is more reliable in virtualized networks.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self

# Clone the kripke repository from its main branch, build it with MPI support,
# and install the executable. This is done in a single RUN command to keep the image clean.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \
    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake, enabling MPI and optimizing for release.
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    # Compile the source code using all available processor cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the compiled executable to a standard system location on the PATH.
    # This avoids using symlinks and makes the application directly runnable.
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    # Clean up the source and build directories to minimize final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# Set a default entrypoint or command for the container.
# Providing a shell is a common practice for HPC application containers
# to allow for interactive inspection or varied execution commands.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Use a standard Ubuntu base image with build tools
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installation to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# FIX: The Kripke dependency 'raja' requires CMake 3.23+. The version in Ubuntu 22.04's
# repository (3.22.1) is insufficient. We must manually download and install a newer version.
ENV CMAKE_VERSION=3.27.9

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, and wget for downloading CMake.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    wget && \
    # Use the build-in TARGETARCH variable for robust multi-platform builds.
    case ${TARGETARCH} in \
         "amd64")  CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"   ;; \
         "arm64")  CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"  ;; \
    esac && \
    # Download the specified CMake version from the official GitHub releases page.
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.sh -O cmake-install.sh && \
    chmod +x cmake-install.sh && \
    # Install to /usr/local which is on the PATH and cleanup the installer.
    ./cmake-install.sh --prefix=/usr/local --skip-license && \
    rm cmake-install.sh && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce layer size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings allow MPI to run as the root user and oversubscribe resources,
# which are common scenarios within containers.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
# Force TCP communication for MPI, which is more reliable in virtualized networks.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self

# Clone the kripke repository from its main branch, build it with MPI support,
# and install the executable. This is done in a single RUN command to keep the image clean.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \
    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake, enabling MPI and optimizing for release.
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    # Compile the source code using all available processor cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the compiled executable to a standard system location on the PATH.
    # This avoids using symlinks and makes the application directly runnable.
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    # Clean up the source and build directories to minimize final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# Set a default entrypoint or command for the container.
# Providing a shell is a common practice for HPC application containers
# to allow for interactive inspection or varied execution commands.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Use a standard Ubuntu base image with build tools
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installation to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Set a recent, stable CMake version. Kripke's dependency (RAJA) requires
# CMake 3.23+, which is newer than the version in Ubuntu 22.04 repositories.
ENV CMAKE_VERSION=3.27.9

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, and wget for downloading CMake.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    wget && \
    # Use the build-in TARGETARCH variable for robust multi-platform builds.
    case ${TARGETARCH} in \
         "amd64")  CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"   ;; \
         "arm64")  CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"  ;; \
    esac && \
    # Download the specified CMake version from the official GitHub releases page.
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.sh -O cmake-install.sh && \
    chmod +x cmake-install.sh && \
    # Install to /usr/local which is on the PATH and cleanup the installer.
    ./cmake-install.sh --prefix=/usr/local --skip-license && \
    rm cmake-install.sh && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce layer size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings allow MPI to run as the root user and oversubscribe resources,
# which are common scenarios within containers.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
# Force TCP communication for MPI, which is more reliable in virtualized networks.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self

# Clone the kripke repository from its main branch, build it with MPI support,
# and install the executable. This is done in a single RUN command to keep the image clean.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \
    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake, enabling MPI and optimizing for release.
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    # Compile the source code using all available processor cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the compiled executable to a standard system location on the PATH.
    # This avoids using symlinks and makes the application directly runnable.
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    # Clean up the source and build directories to minimize final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# Set a default entrypoint or command for the container.
# Providing a shell is a common practice for HPC application containers
# to allow for interactive inspection or varied execution commands.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Use a standard Ubuntu base image with build tools
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installation to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Set a recent, stable CMake version. Kripke's dependency (RAJA) requires
# CMake 3.23+, which is newer than the version in Ubuntu 22.04 repositories.
ENV CMAKE_VERSION=3.27.9

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, and wget for downloading CMake.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    wget && \
    # Use the build-in TARGETARCH variable for robust multi-platform builds.
    case ${TARGETARCH} in \
         "amd64")  CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"   ;; \
         "arm64")  CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"  ;; \
    esac && \
    # Download the specified CMake version from the official GitHub releases page.
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.sh -O cmake-install.sh && \
    chmod +x cmake-install.sh && \
    # Install to /usr/local which is on the PATH and cleanup the installer.
    ./cmake-install.sh --prefix=/usr/local --skip-license && \
    rm cmake-install.sh && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce layer size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings allow MPI to run as the root user and oversubscribe resources,
# which are common scenarios within containers.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
# Force TCP communication for MPI, which is more reliable in virtualized networks.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self

# Clone the kripke repository from its main branch, build it with MPI support,
# and install the executable. This is done in a single RUN command to keep the image clean.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \
    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake, enabling MPI and optimizing for release.
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    # Compile the source code using all available processor cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the compiled executable to a standard system location on the PATH.
    # This avoids using symlinks and makes the application directly runnable.
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    # Clean up the source and build directories to minimize final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# Set a default entrypoint or command for the container.
# Providing a shell is a common practice for HPC application containers
# to allow for interactive inspection or varied execution commands.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

66# to allow for interactive inspection or varied execution commands.
67CMD ["/bin/bash"]
 
# Use a standard Ubuntu base image with build tools
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installation to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Set a recent, stable CMake version. Kripke's dependency (RAJA) requires
# CMake 3.23+, which is newer than the version in Ubuntu 22.04 repositories.
ENV CMAKE_VERSION=3.27.9

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, and wget for downloading CMake.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    wget && \
    # Use the build-in TARGETARCH variable for robust multi-platform builds.
    case ${TARGETARCH} in \
         "amd64")  CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"   ;; \
         "arm64")  CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"  ;; \
    esac && \
    # Download the specified CMake version from the official GitHub releases page.
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.sh -O cmake-install.sh && \
    chmod +x cmake-install.sh && \
    # Install to /usr/local which is on the PATH and cleanup the installer.
    ./cmake-install.sh --prefix=/usr/local --skip-license && \
    rm cmake-install.sh && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce layer size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings allow MPI to run as the root user and oversubscribe resources,
# which are common scenarios within containers.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
# Force TCP communication for MPI, which is more reliable in virtualized networks.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self

# Clone the kripke repository from its main branch, build it with MPI support,
# and install the executable. This is done in a single RUN command to keep the image clean.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \
    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake, enabling MPI and optimizing for release.
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    # Compile the source code using all available processor cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the compiled executable to a standard system location on the PATH.
    # This avoids using symlinks and makes the application directly runnable.
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    # Clean up the source and build directories to minimize final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# Set a default entrypoint or command for the container.
# Providing a shell is a common practice for HPC application containers
# to allow for interactive inspection or varied execution commands.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Use a standard Ubuntu base image with build tools
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installation to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Set a recent, stable CMake version. Kripke's dependency (RAJA) requires
# CMake 3.23+, which is newer than the version in Ubuntu 22.04 repositories.
ENV CMAKE_VERSION=3.27.9

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, and wget for downloading CMake.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    wget && \
    # Use the build-in TARGETARCH variable for robust multi-platform builds.
    case ${TARGETARCH} in \
         "amd64")  CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"   ;; \
         "arm64")  CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"  ;; \
    esac && \
    # Download the specified CMake version from the official GitHub releases page.
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.sh -O cmake-install.sh && \
    chmod +x cmake-install.sh && \
    # Install to /usr/local which is on the PATH and cleanup the installer.
    ./cmake-install.sh --prefix=/usr/local --skip-license && \
    rm cmake-install.sh && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce layer size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings allow MPI to run as the root user and oversubscribe resources,
# which are common scenarios within containers.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
# Force TCP communication for MPI, which is more reliable in virtualized networks.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self

# Clone the kripke repository from its main branch, build it with MPI support,
# and install the executable. This is done in a single RUN command to keep the image clean.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \
    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake, enabling MPI and optimizing for release.
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    # Compile the source code using all available processor cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the compiled executable to a standard system location on the PATH.
    # This avoids using symlinks and makes the application directly runnable.
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    # Clean up the source and build directories to minimize final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# Set a default entrypoint or command for the container.
# Providing a shell is a common practice for HPC application containers
# to allow for interactive inspection or varied execution commands.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

52      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
53      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
54      .. && \
55    # Compile the source code using all available processor cores.
56    make -j$(nproc) && \
57    # Copy the compiled executable to a standard system location on the PATH.

64# Set a default entrypoint or command for the container.
65# Providing a shell is a common practice for HPC application containers
66# to allow for interactive inspection or varied execution commands.

# Use a standard Ubuntu base image with build tools
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installation to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Set a recent, stable CMake version. Kripke's dependency (RAJA) requires
# CMake 3.23+, which is newer than the version in Ubuntu 22.04 repositories.
ENV CMAKE_VERSION=3.27.9

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, and wget for downloading CMake.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    wget && \
    # Use the build-in TARGETARCH variable for robust multi-platform builds.
    case ${TARGETARCH} in \
         "amd64")  CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"   ;; \
         "arm64")  CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"  ;; \
    esac && \
    # Download the specified CMake version from the official GitHub releases page.
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.sh -O cmake-install.sh && \
    chmod +x cmake-install.sh && \
    # Install to /usr/local which is on the PATH and cleanup the installer.
    ./cmake-install.sh --prefix=/usr/local --skip-license && \
    rm cmake-install.sh && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce layer size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings allow MPI to run as the root user and oversubscribe resources,
# which are common scenarios within containers.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
# Force TCP communication for MPI, which is more reliable in virtualized networks.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self

# Clone the kripke repository from its main branch, build it with MPI support,
# and install the executable. This is done in a single RUN command to keep the image clean.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/kripke.git /opt/kripke_src && \
    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake, enabling MPI and optimizing for release.
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    # Compile the source code using all available processor cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the compiled executable to a standard system location on the PATH.
    # This avoids using symlinks and makes the application directly runnable.
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    # Clean up the source and build directories to minimize final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# Set a default entrypoint or command for the container.
# Providing a shell is a common practice for HPC application containers
# to allow for interactive inspection or varied execution commands.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]
